3.0.0.en: The Jews prayed three times a day: the third hour (9 a.m.), the sixth (12 noon) and the ninth (3 p.m.). The early Church in its beginning prayed at the same times in Solomon's Porch at the Temple, though of course without taking part in its sacrifices, until the prayers of the Agpeya and other Church prayers became settled in about the fourth century. Peter and John: these two disciples were joined together from the beginning of Christ's call to them and in special events such as the Transfiguration, the raising of Jairus' daughter, the Garden of Gethsemane and the Sea of Tiberias. The ninth hour: the hour at which Christ gave up the Spirit and completed our redemption, so we go out in it to preach by His power, which is able to work miracles.

3.1.0.en: At the gate of the Temple there was a man lame from his mother's womb, that is, born unable to walk, who was then more than forty years old. His family would carry him and set him at the "Beautiful" gate of the Temple to beg all day long, as is the custom of the poor at the entrances of houses of worship. The Beautiful Gate is the most beautiful of the nine gates that were in the Temple, and this gate was made of bronze and overlaid with gold leaf. Its location was on the eastern side of the Temple between the court of judgment and the court of the Gentiles. Because of the beauty of its appearance, most of those coming to the Temple preferred to enter by it, which is why the lame man sat there to seek his livelihood.

3.2.0.en: Peter and John saw the lame man, and he asked them for alms as usual, since he did not know them and did not expect healing from them.

3.3.0.en: The two Apostles looked intently at him and asked him to fix his gaze and thought on what would be given to him. It was not merely alms but something greater, namely healing and faith.

3.4.0.en: The man thought that he would receive a large sum of money in alms.

3.5.0.en: They had no money, because Christ did not promise His children that He would give them money, but precious spiritual blessings that money cannot buy. The two Apostles used the power of Christ and asked for his healing in His name.

3.5.1.en: Here we note the difference between the miracles of Christ, which He worked by His direct command, and the miracles of the saints, which they work in the name of the Lord.

3.5.2.en: The lack of money with you does not mean that you cannot give, for Chrysostom says: The woman had two mites with which she bought the Kingdom. And do you not have two eyes, two feet and two hands?

3.5.3.en: Almsgiving can be a deed or a word, and not money only.

3.6.0.en: He took him: this shows God's help, the tenderness of the two Apostles and the power of support for everyone in need.

3.6.1.en: His feet and ankle bones received strength: this shows the obedience of the lame man and his will to carry out what the two Apostles commanded him, so he felt a power flowing in his muscles when he tried to rise, and he was able to stand, and even walk and leap. Leaping: jumping with joy, and he entered the Temple amid the crowd of those gathered to offer the evening sacrifice at the ninth hour.

3.6.2.en: The miracle was accomplished immediately. After his healing the man was amazed, and began to walk and leap and thank God for what He had done with him, and he also clung to the company of the two Apostles.

3.7.0.en: The miracle became clear to everyone, because the crowd saw him walking and thanking God, especially since those present had known for many years that he was lame; so they were bewildered and greatly astonished, asking how this had happened to him.

3.7.1.en: Thus the saying of Isaiah about the miracles of the New Testament is fulfilled: "Then shall the lame man leap as an hart" (Isa 35:6).

3.7.2.en: "The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10). So we have protection and strength by repeating it always in prayer - "My Lord Jesus Christ, help me" - and He gives us blessing and salvation, protects us from the wars of the devil and gives us strength to overcome difficulties.

3.8.0.en: Solomon's Porch: a large colonnade running along the back (eastern) wall of the Temple, with 162 columns.

3.8.1.en: After his healing the man clung to the two Apostles, in acknowledgment of their kindness and to learn from them about the Lord Jesus, in whom he had newly believed. All entered Solomon's Porch, and great crowds from the Temple and the city followed them when they heard the news. His presence with the two Apostles was a proclamation of the miracle and a preaching of the power of Christ, which is able to do all things.

3.9.0.en: The Apostle Peter seized the opportunity of the gathering of many to see the miracle, and at once answered the questions of the people, and stressed emphatically that he and John were not the authors of the miracle of healing, but the Lord Jesus Christ Himself, who is one with His good Father.

3.9.1.en: If you do something good and others praise you for it, thank God and turn the glory to Him, so that all hearts may be attached to Him, and you disappear and He appears.

3.10.0.en: The God of our fathers: that is, the God known in the Old Testament to all the Jews. And Jesus Christ is His Son, and not a prophet or merely an ordinary person. So he proclaims the divinity of Christ, His redemption and the need to believe in His salvation.

3.10.1.en: Glorified His Son: by His Resurrection and Ascension.

3.10.2.en: You denied Him in the presence of Pilate: that is, your insistence on rejecting Christ, although His miracles and His words proclaim His divinity, and even Pilate himself testified to His innocence.

3.10.3.en: He told them that the God of the fathers - Abraham, Isaac and Jacob - from whose descendants these hearers came, has glorified His Son Jesus in the healing of the lame man in His name. And this Jesus is the one they refused to believe in, and they refused to let Pilate release Him, though he had satisfied himself of His innocence when he tried Him.

3.11.0.en: The Jews asked that Barabbas the murderer be released to them instead of Jesus, when Pilate offered them the release of Christ on the occasion of the Feast of Passover.

3.12.0.en: Thus they held fast to a murderer, Barabbas, and rejected the Source of life and demanded His death. But the Father raised Him from the dead, which the Apostles bear witness to, for they saw Him with their own eyes after His Resurrection, and ate and lived with Him for forty days.

3.12.1.en: Raised from the dead: this is a proclamation of His divinity and that He is the Source of life, whereas they preferred the taker of life, that is, Barabbas.

3.12.2.en: Here we see the central place of the Resurrection in preaching, since there is no Christianity without the Resurrection. We also see the Apostles' complete denial of themselves and their seeking only the glory of Christ.

3.13.0.en: Through faith in His name: the faith of the two Apostles and likewise the faith of the lame man.

3.13.1.en: Perfect soundness: that is, the strength of the two legs that for more than forty years had been unable to stand or walk. The Apostle Peter declares that the basis of the accomplishment of the miracle is faith, in order to call the hearers to faith in Christ the Savior, who is able to heal our diseases and solve all our problems.

3.14.0.en: He gently makes an excuse for them because they were ignorant of the person of Christ, since they and their rulers demanded His crucifixion. For the preacher is careful to remove the spirit of despair from the soul of the hearer, lest he despair of himself, and to make it easy for him to come to repentance so that his sins are forgiven.

3.15.0.en: What they did was useful for the fulfillment of God's counsel concerning the salvation of mankind, which all the prophets of the Old Testament foretold, especially Isaiah, who saw by the spirit of prophecy the Lord wounded for our transgressions (Isa 53:5). Thus the Father, the Maker of good things, turned the evil of the Jews into salvation and good.

3.16.0.en: What is required of them now, and likewise of us, is repentance and turning back from walking in evil, and confession of the faith, so that they may receive Baptism and their sins be forgiven, as the list of debts is blotted out when they are paid. And the times of refreshing come from the presence of God, because the Jews imagined that the coming of Christ would bring material relief and deliverance from the hand of the Romans. But what is meant here is spiritual refreshing by being delivered from the hand of Satan.

3.17.0.en: He shall send: what is meant is either the Incarnation of Christ to give us salvation in the New Testament so that we live by faith in Him, or His Second Coming to take His children and glorify them with Him in heaven. Which before was preached: that is, the One of whom the prophets of old prophesied that He would come and save the world.

3.18.0.en: Heaven must receive Him: the Jews believed that the Christ would remain on earth forever, that is, that He would not die, so they wondered at His words about the necessity of His death (Jn 12:34). Peter explained that Christ remains alive forever, but in heaven and not on earth.

3.18.1.en: The times of restitution of all things: that is, the spread of the proclamation of Christ in the whole world and the faith of many. It does not mean that by restitution of all things every soul will be received, but those appointed by God and prepared for salvation. Christ ascended to the Father and is in heaven until the end of the times arrives, in which the world returns to the knowledge of Christ and faith in Him (1 Cor 15:25), and then after that comes His Second Coming at the end of the world, as the holy prophets foretold.

3.19.0.en: The Apostle pointed to the prophecy of Moses the prophet about the Lord Christ in (Deut 18:18), who comes as a prophet, that is, one who makes known the will of the Father for the salvation of the world, and as being like Moses in respect of:

3.19.2.en: 2- His bringing the law of the New Testament, as Moses brought the law of the Old Testament.

3.19.3.en: 3- His delivering His people from the hand of Satan, as Moses delivered the people from the bondage of Pharaoh.

3.19.4.en: 4- His atoning intercession for His people, like Moses' pleading intercession for the Jews many times so that God would not destroy them in their murmurings in the wilderness.

3.19.5.en: Moses asked them to believe in Christ and listen to His message, because they believe that they are the sons of Moses, so it is necessary for them to believe in Christ, of whom he prophesied among them, and not to oppose Him and despise Him as they said to the man born blind (Jn 9:28, 29).

3.20.0.en: For whoever does not hear Christ is deprived of membership in the new people of God, that is, the Church, and will have no inheritance in the Kingdom, that is, he perishes. He proclaimed the punishment of unbelief in order to call them to repentance and salvation.

3.21.0.en: He also affirmed that Samuel, who was the first prophet after Moses and who founded the school of the prophets, also prophesied about the Lord, he and all who came after him of the prophets of the Old Testament up to John the Baptist, and their prophecies included the descent of the Holy Spirit and the working of the miracles that take place in the days of the New Testament.

3.22.0.en: Children of the prophets: that is, followers, so they must believe what the prophets foretold about Christ.

3.22.1.en: Your seed: that is, Christ, as the Apostle Paul explained (Gal 3:16), and he urged them, as children of the covenant that God gave of old to Abraham their father, by the coming of Christ from his seed, blessing and saving all people, Jews and Gentiles.

3.23.0.en: The Jews had priority in receiving faith in the coming of Christ to them first, before the Gentiles, so that through faith in Him they might receive the spiritual blessings that make them leave their sins for a life of repentance. This sermon resembles the sermon of Pentecost in the following:

3.23.1.en: 1- The proof that Jesus of Nazareth is the awaited Messiah.

3.23.2.en: 2- The showing of the sin of the Jews in rejecting Christ.

3.23.3.en: 3- A call to repentance to receive the mercy of God and to believe in Christ.

3.23.4.en: All of us are exposed to sin, but we are distinguished from others by repentance, returning to God and repairing what we have spoiled by our sins.

3.23.5.en: May we not oppose the guidance others give us, nor what we hear in the Church and the Holy Bible, for they are personal messages that call us to repentance and rescue us from error.

3.23.6.en: Let us have daily repentance that renews our life and restores our spiritual zeal, and let us complete it in the sacrament of Confession, so that we always live by repentance and receive our salvation.

3.23.7.en: The trial of Peter and John, the power of prayer and the life of the first Church

4.0.s.en: (1) The imprisonment of the two Apostles

4.0.0.en: The priests: they had authority to permit or forbid teaching in the Temple to whomever they wished.

4.0.1.en: The news of the preaching inside Solomon's Porch reached the priests, so they came at once, and with them the captain of the Temple guard and his soldiers, who were Jewish Levites and not Romans.

4.0.2.en: The Sadducees also came, who do not believe in the Resurrection, and because they regarded what the Apostles said about the Resurrection of Christ as an attack on their beliefs, they were the fiercest opponents of the Apostles' preaching. All of them were displeased at the spread of the news of the Resurrection of Christ, which they had tried to conceal by bribing the Roman soldiers at the tomb.

4.1.0.en: They seized the two Apostles, and since they wanted to gather the seventy elders, the members of the supreme Jewish council, the "Sanhedrin," some of whom lived outside Jerusalem, they put the Apostles in custody until the next day so that the gathering of the members could be completed.

4.2.0.en: The opposition of the priests and Sadducees did not stop the effect of the two Apostles' proclamation on the people, for the number of believers increased and became five thousand men, and this rapid growth of the Church was a clear fruit of the Holy Spirit.

4.2.1.en: Do not be disturbed by the opposition of the wicked, but hold fast to your principles and the commandments of Christ, for their mockery and opposition, however strong it may seem, is a test of your faith and steadfastness, and trust in God's blessing on your personal life and even in the effect of your words and conduct on others, though it be after a while.

4.3.s.en: (2) The trial of Peter and John

4.3.0.en: The next day the three groups that make up the council gathered, namely: the rulers, that is, the priests; the elders, that is, the heads of the clans; and the scribes, that is, the scholars and teachers. They gathered in Jerusalem to try the two Apostles.

4.4.0.en: And Annas was with them: the former high priest, whom the Romans had removed.

4.4.2.en: John and Alexander: relatives of the high priest and men of standing in Jerusalem.

4.4.3.en: The kindred of the high priest: five high priests came out of it, so it was a distinguished clan, and from it, accordingly, came a large number of members of the Sanhedrin.

4.4.4.en: All these gathered to stop the preaching of the risen Christ, because this would reveal their wickedness in condemning Christ to death.

4.5.0.en: They set the two Apostles in the midst, and the question was repeated about the source of the power that worked the miracle and about the name by which the miracle was accomplished. This was not because they did not know the answer, but so that they might find in the answer an opportunity to seize on against the Apostles in order to punish them, regarding the use of the name of Christ as a kind of blasphemy or sorcery. The purpose of setting them in the midst and questioning them was to intimidate them so that they would stop their preaching.

4.6.0.en: Here the Lord's promise in (Mt 10:19-20) is fulfilled, that when a Christian is tried for the faith the Holy Spirit speaks on his tongue.

4.6.1.en: Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit and went straight to the subject with all courage, to make up for his denial of the Lord during the trial at the high priest's house, and he addressed them with the respect due to them.

4.7.0.en: A good deed: trials are held because of a wrong, but now it is held because of a good deed and help done to another, and this shows the wickedness of the Sanhedrin.

4.7.1.en: This is because the lame man who was healed was present at the trial.

4.7.2.en: They must know, and all the Jews with them, that the name of the Lord Jesus, who is the Christ, the awaited Messiah, who is of Nazareth, as they wrote on His cross, and who rose from the dead by the power of the Father against their plan, this name is what healed the sick man. So Peter, who was foremost in speaking, expressing his own opinion and John's, showed three basic matters that call the hearers to faith, which are:

4.7.3.en: 1- Jesus of Nazareth is the Christ.

4.7.4.en: 2- Their sin in condemning Him to the cross.

4.7.5.en: 3- In the name of Christ the lame man was healed and stood, and he is standing before them now.

4.8.0.en: The chief cornerstone: it is the highest stone in any arch or dome bearing a roof, upon which falls all the pressure from the stones of the arch on its right or its left, so that the arch does not collapse. Or it is the stone that joins two walls meeting at a right angle.

4.8.1.en: What is meant is that Christ is the foundation of salvation for mankind, and none other.

4.8.2.en: The builders: the members of the council of the seventy, who were responsible for the spiritual building of the Jews, and who ought to have been the first to believe in Christ so as to lead the people in the way of faith.

4.8.3.en: Peter completed his preaching to them. We note that he does not defend himself or John but preaches the Lord, pointing out their error, which the Psalm (Ps 118:22) mentioned, in rejecting faith in Christ Jesus and despising Him, whereas God made Him the chief cornerstone in the cause of the accomplishment of salvation.

4.9.0.en: Christ alone is the Savior and He alone is the One anointed by God to accomplish salvation, for He alone possesses the atoning intercession that forgives the sins of His people and atones for their evils.

4.10.0.en: They marveled greatly at the power of the preaching, and the mention of the boldness of John is noted, so it is understood implicitly that he supported Peter's words with words and gestures proclaiming his faith, although the two Apostles had not been taught under the teachers of the Jews or in their religious schools, but were of the common people. From this the chief priests remembered that the two Apostles had been with Christ, and had seen them with Him before, so He is the source of their knowledge and eloquence.

4.11.0.en: The presence of the sick man who was healed left them no opportunity to oppose the two Apostles, and the judges became the accused in their opposition to Christ.

4.12.0.en: They had them taken out of the council to confer and issue the verdict, and instead of asking themselves what to do about their own salvation and their attitude toward this preaching, they concentrated their wickedness on how and what to do with the Apostles, now that the effect of this clear sign had reached the minds of the people of Jerusalem.

4.12.1.en: So a man grows hardened by sin when he becomes accustomed to it. What they did to Christ of injustice they wanted to apply to the Apostles, because their personal dignity was what they were after, not the truth. So if your error becomes apparent, do not continue to resist or to justify yourself, but return to God in prayer that He may reveal the truth to you, so that you repent and correct your mistakes, following the example of Saul of Tarsus, who obeyed and became the great Apostle Paul.

4.13.0.en: They decided to threaten them so that they would be afraid to resume preaching among the people and would not mention the name of Jesus, which they could not even bear to pronounce with their mouths. For, being unable to find any charge against them, they used threats to frighten them.

4.14.0.en: They brought them back into the session and charged them not to repeat such preaching in the future.

4.15.0.en: But the two Apostles replied that God must be obeyed rather than men, and it is He who commands them to preach the Gospel to the whole world, and therefore they cannot keep silent about what they had seen or heard in the days of Christ's companionship with them. Here appear:

4.15.1.en: 1- The evil purposes of the council against the commands of God.

4.15.2.en: 2- The obedience of the two Apostles to God and their strength in holding to the truth, whatever the opposition.

4.16.0.en: So they were released without punishment for fear of the people, who were glorifying God for the miracle, especially since this man had been sick for more than forty years. The length of the illness and the inability of human medicine to cure it shows the power of the miracle.

4.16.1.en: And so the council had nothing but threats, because it was powerless before the power of God.

4.16.2.en: The clear truths of God are before us, but our pride prevents us from confessing our sins and accepting the saving work of God in us. It is our duty not to lose the opportunity like these rulers, who lived in the illusion of putting an end to the preaching rather than responding to it.

4.17.0.en: After their release the two Apostles returned to the Apostles and the rest of the believers and told them what had happened, to strengthen their faith, to thank God and to rejoice in His work in His Church.

4.18.0.en: In view of their great need of God's help, they prayed fervently, calling upon God the Creator of all things and the One able to protect His children, as we address Him in the Liturgy with this prayer, "that He is the Creator of all that exists." Thus we see that prayer is the greatest solution to man's weakness and problems.

4.18.1.en: For as long as God is the Creator of the universe and its Ruler, our hearts are reassured, whatever the threats of the wicked. This prayer is also a prayer of thanksgiving to God for His great grace and His rescue of His Apostles.

4.19.0.en: Those gathered prayed to God, who said by the mouth of David the prophet in the Psalm (Ps 2:1, 2) that many would rise up against Christ with their thoughts and their opposing deeds, whether rulers or kings, stubbornly resisting the Lord (the Father) and His Christ (the Son). This is what happened with the rulers of the Jews in their opposition to Christ and the Apostles, and this shows the power of God and the weakness of the rulers of the world and their turmoil because of the evil in their hearts, and the failure of all their plots, because God is stronger than they: if they crucify Christ, He rises on the third day victorious, and if they seize the Apostles, they find no charge against them, but the miracle spreads and draws many to faith.

4.20.0.en: Were gathered together against Your holy Child: this was fulfilled before the two Apostles in what they saw of the priests and the council of the Jews moving against Christ, together with Herod and Pilate and many of the Gentiles and Jews. But God, the Ruler of all, allowed what happened because it was the accomplishment of His plan for the salvation of mankind.

4.21.0.en: They did not ask the Lord to protect them, but to strengthen them for the success of the preaching with all clarity and boldness. This shows their great attachment to Christ the Savior and their faith in Him and their desire to spread the faith, so they do not think of themselves but ask for power by which to glorify God.

4.22.0.en: They also asked Him to support them with other miracles of healing and signs confirming the truth of their preaching, and wonders bearing witness to the greatness of the name of Christ, the Holy One, the Son of the Great God.

4.23.0.en: Then a visible sign appeared of the acceptance of their prayer by God, which was the shaking of the place and the filling of those present with the Spirit, that is, the Holy Spirit gave them strength to continue and work, and they received zeal and power to proclaim the name of Christ and preach Him.

4.23.1.en: The first descent, for the beginning of the Spirit's dwelling in man, is not repeated, but the filling, to renew his activity and work, can be repeated many times in proportion to the purity of man's soul and his asking for the filling from God.

4.23.2.en: Take refuge in God through prayer in all your needs, confident of His support.

4.23.3.en: Thank Him for His gifts and ask for more for His name's sake, and you will receive abundantly, for He is rich and loves His children and will help you to show His name in your life and your words.

4.24.s.en: (4) The life of the first Church

4.24.0.en: Here he calls the believers a multitude, since they had increased beyond the five thousand mentioned before, but all had the unity of the one Holy Spirit, the leader and guide of each individual and of the whole group. They still lived by the principle of common ownership without selfishness, for each one felt that his money belonged to the Church and to all in it.

4.25.0.en: The Spirit was working in the Apostles with power to preach the Resurrection of Christ, which is the foundation of faith in Christ the Savior. As for the great grace that came upon them all, it gave their preaching an extraordinary power and penetration in the hearts of the hearers, who saw them in intense love, for there was not one poor person among them but complete harmony between rich and poor, as the owners of fields and possessions hastened to sell them to meet the needs of those in need.

4.26.0.en: Laying the money at the feet of the Apostles was a figure of the believers' lack of concern for it, for their hearts were occupied with the spiritual life, while material needs were of less importance, and all money was counted as nothing before faith and life with God. So money was used to meet the needs of all according to each one's situation.

4.27.0.en: This also included one of the well-known servants, Joseph, the uncle of the Apostle St. Mark, whom the Apostles called Barnabas, that is, son of exhortation, because of the eloquence and the moving words that distinguished him among the hearers. He was originally of the tribe of Levi, among those living abroad in Cyprus, and he owned a field, which he sold and gave its price to the Apostle Fathers.

4.27.1.en: May you feel for the needy around you and know well that all the money and possessions you have belong to God, who appointed you steward over them to meet your needs and the needs of those around you. You are a member of the Body of Christ, which is the Church, so do not shut up your compassion from any person in need.

4.27.2.en: The growth of the Church and the trials
